result.summary: Replaced the stub in fusion.py with a real Reciprocal Rank Fusion implementation. scores(rankings, k=60) sums 1/(k+rank) per document with rank starting at 1, using first-occurrence positions only within each list so duplicates do not shift later positions, and omitting documents with no contribution. fuse(rankings, k=60, limit=None) shares the same scoring helper, orders by descending score with ascending string ID tie-breaks, applies limit when not None, and never mutates inputs. Validation of k (finite positive int/float, not bool, rejecting NaN/inf/0/negatives/strings/None) and limit (None or nonnegative non-bool int) runs before any iteration so errors surface deterministically. Rankings are materialized once via list(rankings), so generators work. search_app.py was not modified and its caller contract is preserved.
findings: All 8 acceptance checks pass, including hand-calculated scores, duplicate-position retention, ties, limits, empty inputs, validation errors, generator inputs, and non-mutation.
The existing search_app.search_results caller is untouched and still returns {'documents': [...], 'method': 'fusion'} with fuse called as fuse([keyword_ids, semantic_ids], limit=limit).
Validation happens before list(rankings) consumption in both functions, so invalid k/limit errors are deterministic even for one-shot iterables.
Synthetic nDCG3 metrics are reported for four toy queries; these are illustrative only and not a reproduction of the paper's TREC/LETOR results.
evidence: fusion.py now defines scores and fuse delegating to a shared _score_map helper implementing 1/(k+rank) with first-occurrence positions.

run_checks output: 'Ran 8 tests ... OK' with all named tests (test_existing_caller, test_hand_calculated_scores, test_duplicates_preserve_original_positions, test_ties, test_limits, test_empty, test_invalid_k, test_default_and_custom_k) passing.
search_app.py read and left unmodified; integration verified by the passing test_existing_caller.
